s1.syndrome_frame: A congenital, slowly growing, exophytic oral lesion
salient_findings: 1.5-cm diameter, exophytic, smooth, regular, and soft lesion on the midline of the dorsal tongue
Lesion present since birth with no change in size or character
Mild contrast enhancement on MRI with intact overlying mucosa
key_facts: 20-year-old man with no significant medical history
Lesion located on the midline of the dorsal tongue
Lesion is 1.5-cm in diameter
Lesion is exophytic, smooth, regular, and soft
Lesion has been present since birth
Lesion has not changed in size or character over time
Vital signs are within normal limits
MRI shows a 1.5-cm protuberant mass arising from the dorsal aspect of the tongue
Lesion appears partly fatty and likely submucosal on MRI
Intact overlying mucosa on MRI
No involvement of intrinsic tongue muscles on MRI
Sublingual space and major salivary glands appear normal on MRI

shortlist.label: Congenital granular cell epulis
shortlist.why_kept: Congenital, exophytic, and partly fatty characteristics match the case

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Partly fatty appearance on MRI and soft texture are consistent with lipoma

shortlist.label: Dermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Congenital origin and submucosal location are plausible for dermoid cyst

shortlist.label: Hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign, congenital, and exophytic characteristics are consistent with hamartoma

shortlist.label: Choristoma
shortlist.why_kept: Congenital, benign, and partly fatty characteristics are consistent with choristoma

raw.rationale: The lesion's location on the midline of the dorsal tongue, its exophytic and smooth appearance, and its presence since birth are consistent with congenital granular cell epulis, a rare benign tumor that typically occurs on the tongue in newborns or young children.

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: While the lesion appears partly fatty on MRI, lipomas are not typically found on the tongue and do not usually present at birth.

rejected.label: Dermoid cyst
rejected.why: Dermoid cysts can occur on the tongue but are not typically exophytic or smooth, and often contain elements like hair or teeth.

rejected.label: Hamartoma
rejected.why: Hamartomas are benign tumors that can occur on the tongue, but they are not typically described as exophytic, smooth, and regular.

rejected.label: Choristoma
rejected.why: Choristomas are rare benign tumors that contain normal tissue in an abnormal location, but they are not typically found on the tongue or described as exophytic and smooth.
